status_summary: Congress enacted the DPC and HSA changes in Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04), and the IRS explained them in Notice 2026-5, released 2025-12-09. Beginning in months after 2025-12-31, a qualifying DPC arrangement (primary care only, fixed periodic fee up to $150 a month per person or $300 for more than one person) does not disqualify a person from contributing to an HSA, and HSA funds can pay its fees; bronze and catastrophic marketplace plans are treated as HSA-compatible high-deductible plans; and the telehealth safe harbor became permanent. This record does not cover the same section's recommendations on short-term plans, association health plans and individual coverage HRAs; Federal Register queries found no rule or proposal on short-term plans or association health plans since 2025-01-20. HHS's 2027 payment notice (final, published 2026-05-20) separately revises catastrophic plan standards and implements provisions of the 2025 law.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed; sections 71306 to 71308 make the telehealth safe harbor for high-deductible plans permanent, treat bronze and catastrophic marketplace plans as HSA-compatible, and provide that qualifying direct primary care arrangements do not bar HSA contributions.

The IRS releases Notice 2026-5 (Expanded Availability of Health Savings Accounts under the One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act), explaining the DPC rules (primary care services only, fixed periodic fee capped at $150 a month per individual or $300 for several people), the bronze and catastrophic plan rule, and the permanent telehealth safe harbor; comments requested by 2026-03-06.
The DPC and bronze/catastrophic plan provisions apply to months beginning after 2025-12-31; the telehealth safe harbor applies retroactively to plan years beginning after 2024-12-31.

HHS finalizes the 2027 payment notice (FR doc. 2026-10050), which adds cost-sharing flexibilities for catastrophic and bronze plans and allows catastrophic plans with terms of up to 10 years, and implements provisions of the 2025 law.
